newsitem.title: TANZANIA: U.S., Koreans buy Tanzania tobacco, cable assets.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Koreans buy Tanzania tobacco, cable assets.

text.p: Tanzania's privatisation agency sold state assets worth $17.6 million in tobacco and cable manufacturing companies last week.
Officials at the Parastatal Sector Reform Commission (PSRC) said the deals were concluded with Universal Leaf Tobacco Co. of the United States and South Korea's Dae Sung Cable Ltd.

The Virginia-based company bought assets worth $16.3 million from the state-run Tanzania Tobacco Board (TTB) while Dae Sung signed a $1.3 million agreement for a 22 percent stake in state-run Tanzania Cables Ltd.
The TTB sale involves the divestiture of Tanzania's sole tobacco processing facility, at Morogoro, and assorted TTB marketing assets, officials said.

Under the terms of the agreement, Universal Leaf Tobacco will invest an additional $8.2 million in plant and equipment to help rehabilitate Tanzania's tobacco-producing sector over the next two years.
The TTB plant processes locally grown tobacco for private exporters and the local cigarette industry. Universal Tobacco is required to operate the mill under the same conditions.
"The factory will still be open to all buyers of raw tobacco, irrespective of who owns it," a PRSC official said.

Industry experts said the mill was a strategic purchase for Universal Leaf Tobacco, which is expected to use Tanzanian tobacco in what the industry terms "American Blend" cigarettes. The U.S. company also buys tobacco from Malawi and Zimbabwe.
Tanzania produces between 20-30 million kilos of tobacco a year in the western Iringa and southern Songea regions.

Under the terms of the cable sale, Dae Sung Cable Ltd becomes the majority shareholder in TCL. It acquires 22 percent of the government's 51 percent shareholding plus another 29 percent divested by a local company, Paper Products Ltd.

A PSRC statement said of the remaining 29 percent government stake in TCL, 14 percent would be divested to Tanzania Development Finance Ltd (TDFL) while 15 percent would be retained for future sale on the Dar es Salaam stock exchange.
